title: One vs multiple businesses: Alex West's sniper, shotgun and fractal strategy
summary: Alex West compares building many products (shotgun) with focusing on one (sniper), using his own record: 20 products in two years before finding Cyber Leads. He argues for shotgun before product-market fit, sniper after, and a "fractal" loop that runs the shotgun on distribution channels whenever growth plateaus.

principles.text: Before you have a product that can change your life, ship many small products fast; each launch closes a feedback loop.
principles.quote: pre-product Market fit so if you don't have that product that has the potential to change your life or get you to where you want to go right if you want to be a billionaire that's different

principles.text: After you find a product that works, go sniper and focus on it; spreading across new products only diluted his income.
principles.quote: when I implemented shotgun after I had cyber leads all I did was spread myself thin and make less money

principles.text: When growth plateaus, run the shotgun on distribution channels, not new products, then focus on the winner.
principles.quote: you go within the business and you you you implement the shortgun strategy in order to build new distribution channels

principles.text: Distribution deserves as much time as product; most founders spend 80-90% on product.
principles.quote: every startup should focus 50% of their time on marketing and 50% of their time on product

principles.text: Launch scrappy: polish does not matter. A landing page and a buy button were enough.
principles.quote: all I needed was a landing page and a buy button

principles.text: One product with several distribution channels is safer than several products sharing one channel.
principles.quote: the best is one product with three channels
